(Nasdaq: PEPG), a clinical-stage biotechnology company pioneering oligonucleotide therapies with the potential to transform the treatment of rare genetic diseases, today announced positive topline results from the 10 mg/kg multiple ascending dose cohort of the ongoing Phase 2 FREEDOM2-DM1 trial ( NCT06667453 ) evaluating PGN-EDODM1 in patients with myotonic dystrophy type 1 (DM1), a rare, progressive, and multisystemic genetic disease.

These forward-looking statements include, without limitation, statements regarding the therapeutic potential and safety profile of PGN-EDODM1 , statements regarding PGN-EDODM1’s potential to deliver meaningful benefit to the DM1 community, evidence of PGN-EDODM1’s potential to address multiple clinical manifestations of DM1 including PepGen’s ambition to change how DM1 is treated, the topline results from the 10 mg/kg multiple ascending dose cohort of the ongoing Phase 2 FREEDOM2-DM1 trial, expectations regarding the timing of data for the 12.5 mg/kg cohort of the FREEDOM2-DM1 trial, the FREEDOM-OLE 10mg/kg safety and 5 mg/kg clinical results, the potential for any functional improvements that may result from splicing correction with PGN-EDODM1, dose-dependent increases in splicing suggesting that PGN-EDODM1 is getting into the muscle and effectively binding to the target, and ongoing and planned regulatory interactions.
